title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Grothendieck. It is page V of a student's write-up, headed 'CORNU Ph., 16/06/78, C4 Math'. It was evidently filed with the Teichmüller notes, perhaps because of the icosahedral/A5 symmetry that occurs in the SL(2,Z/n) and finite-quotient computations on the previous page. The handwriting and the 1978 date differ from Grothendieck's 1981-83 notes.

The mathematics is the classical proof that the rotation group of the icosahedron (equivalently, the dodecahedron) acts on 5 objects. The page proceeds as follows.
- A is the set of 30 edges of the icosahedron.
- Quotienting by the antipodal identification gives Ā = A/(±), with 15 classes. These are identified with a set 𝒞 of 15 'cercles', probably the 15 symmetry planes or great circles, each perpendicular to an antipodal edge pair.
- A map ρ of order 3 is defined, sending an edge in C_a to one in ρ'(C_a). It permutes the classes in packets of 3. Ā splits into 5 such 'paquets' of 3 mutually perpendicular edge-pairs, called 'trièdres' (the 5 inscribed octahedra / orthogonal frames). The set of trihedra is 𝒯 ≅ Ā/(ρ).
- Two edges are 'orthogonal' if they are distinct and lie in the same ρ-orbit. Orthogonal edges share no vertex.
- For a vertex s, let A(s) be the 5 edges at s. The map A(s) → 𝒯 is injective, because two distinct edges at s share s and so cannot be orthogonal (nor antipodal). Since |A(s)| = |𝒯| = 5, it is a bijection.
- This is the standard step toward identifying the icosahedral rotation group with A5 acting on the 5 orthogonal triples. The local bijection at each vertex is used to show the action is faithful or transitive.
errors: The notation is somewhat muddled: ρ is said to map C_a to ρ'(C_a) without defining ρ'; ρ' presumably means ρ^{-1} or ρ^2.
The quotient A/(a) is written loosely; it should denote identification of antipodal edges.
The injectivity argument implicitly also needs that two distinct edges at s are not antipodal; this is trivially true but unstated.
These are minor issues; the argument is otherwise correct.

ideas.what: Partition of the 30 icosahedron edges into 5 sets of 3 mutually orthogonal antipodal pairs, giving the action of the icosahedral group on 5 objects (≅ A5)
ideas.modern_name: Icosahedral group I ≅ A5 via the 5 inscribed octahedra / orthogonal edge-frames
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Vorlesungen über das Ikosaeder, 1884; earlier folklore)

ideas.what: Bijection between the edges at a vertex and the 5 trihedra, proved by injectivity plus cardinality
ideas.modern_name: Vertex stabilizer (C5) acting simply transitively on the 5 frames

deep.surprise_reason: This is a 1978 student exercise (Ph. Cornu, C4 maths) on the classical icosahedron/A5 correspondence, misfiled in the Teichmüller folder. It contains no Grothendieck mathematics and nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The header identifies the author as the student 'CORNU Ph.', dated 16/06/78, page V of the student's document; it is not Grothendieck's text.
'Ā = A/(a)' likely denotes the quotient by the antipodal relation (the underlined a is probably the antipodal map or class), not a quotient by a single element.
The crossed-out phrase after 'Donc Notons' is a struck-through word; the line reads 'Donc Notons Ā = A/(a) ≃ 𝒞'.
The definition of orthogonality is written in three staggered lines on the page; the transcription's ordering ('distinctes et ... même orbite sous ρ') is correct.
